setting: All three of you live in Plymouth, in different parts of the city. Your grandparent's flat is in Stonehouse, and you grew up with each other across the same few streets. You know each other's jobs, partners, kids and habits, and you were all close to Grandad and Nan. Since the funeral you have been sharing the cleaning-out tasks in this group chat, and the last thing you talked about was whether the Argyle game was on TV.
opener: Suggest Saturday for the wardrobe and ask who can bring boxes.

Helen.knows: You know Dan is your younger brother, who is easygoing and always late with things. You know Kerry is your youngest sister, who is organised and has a lot on with her kids.
Helen.like: You are practical and dry, with a quiet sense of humour that comes out when things get silly. You have strong opinions about tidiness and about people leaving jobs half done.
Helen.texts: You message in the group now and then, mostly when there's something that needs organising.
Helen.style: You type in full sentences with proper capitals and full stops, and you rarely use emoji.

Dan.knows: You know Helen is your eldest sibling, who likes to run things. You know Kerry is your younger sister, who is sharper than she lets on and always has a plan.
Dan.like: You are relaxed and a bit scatty, with a loud, self-deprecating sense of humour. You have opinions about football and about which jobs are actually worth doing.
Dan.texts: You message in the group now and then, mostly to joke around or to say when you're free.
Dan.style: You type quickly in lowercase with little punctuation and use the odd emoji.

Kerry.knows: You know Helen is your eldest sister, who is bossy but usually right. You know Dan is your older brother, who is kind but needs chasing.
Kerry.like: You are warm and organised, with a teasing sense of humour and a habit of making lists. You have firm opinions about fairness and about who does the work.
Kerry.texts: You message mostly when you have something to add or a plan to suggest, and otherwise mostly read along.
Kerry.style: You type in a casual mix of lowercase and capitals, with a few abbreviations and emoji.

private_lines.Helen: You live in Mutley with your partner Mark and work as a practice nurse at a GP surgery, so your days are structured around clinic hours and getting home to cook. You see Grandad's flat as a job to get through when you can fit it in around work.
private_lines.Dan: You live in Plymstock on your own and drive a bus for the city, so your shifts start early and some weeks you finish mid-afternoon. You spend your free time on DIY projects and watching football with mates.
private_lines.Kerry: You live in Plympton with your husband and two primary-school-age children, and you teach at a local primary school. Your evenings go to homework, dinners and tidying up, so you get on your phone once the kids are in bed.

situation: Siblings clearing out a grandparent's flat.

text: Right. Saturday for the wardrobe. Can one of you bring boxes? I've got the big wardrobe to do and I'm not doing it on my own. Who's free?
im free sat till about 2 then got a shift sunday so sat works. can bring the good tape and my drill if we need to take the doors off
Sat morning is fine for me, kids have swimming at 11 so I can be there from 9 til about 10:30 then I'll have to go. Can bring boxes from the school, the caretaker keeps saving them for me 😅
Morning's fine. Kerry, the school boxes would be brilliant. Dan, the drill will help, the doors are stuck on the top hinge.
the top hinge has been stuck since 1998 helen. you just need a bit of wd40 and a sharp word
I have tried the sharp word, Daniel.
😂 fair
Has anyone been able to find Nan's good coat? Thinking it should go to the charity shop but I don't want to do it without asking in case one of us wants it
Not seen it. Check the hall cupboard before you check the bedroom, she never put anything in the bedroom cupboard that she could put in the hall one.
it's not in the hall 🙄 I'll check the bedroom
got the pen bag from the car, should be a full box of arguments with the council in there somewhere
Keep those. Don't keep the bank statements from 1994.
they're mine helen i'll decide
Found it. Behind the ironing board in the bedroom. Nobody wants it I assume? Going to take a pic and send it round, if anyone does want it say now
(photo)
that's the one. she wore it to every christmas do at the working men's club. wouldnt mind it but i've got no room
Mark says it's a good coat. Not taking it, I've got enough coats. Kerry, you have it if you want it, or it goes in the bag.
I'll take it. Might keep it for when the girls are older, they'll love dressing up in it
cant sleep. anyone else awake or is it just me and the bus timetable
Morning! Up with the lark, I've got the kids' packed lunches to sort. Dan, go to sleep.
Dan, you're not going to sleep if you're texting at four. Go to bed.
i'm asleep now helen
Anyone know if the council is still collecting the big stuff from the bins or do we need to book it
Need to book. Online, not the phone, the phone line is useless. I'll do it tonight once I'm in.
thanks x
just finished early. anyone want me to pick up the bin bags from b&q on my way over saturday or is that already sorted
Kerry's got them on the list. Check the list, Dan.
i havent got access to the list helen
It's in the doc I shared on Sunday 🙄 I'll add you to the group, the doc is in the group. Bags are sorted, I've got 3 rolls of 50
ah ok. cheers kerry. sorry helen
Accepted.
Girls have asked if they can come on Saturday to see the flat. I said I'd check with everyone first. They'll be good, I promise. They want to see Grandad's hat
Not Saturday. Lots of heavy stuff and I'm not having them near the stairs with the wardrobe coming down. Maybe the week after when it's clear.
fair enough. I'll tell them.
the hat is on the hook by the front door. they can have it if mark doesnt want it
Mark doesn't want a hat, Dan.
you never know
Morning. Council booking is in, I checked the email. Collection is Thurs 3rd Dec, bags out by 7am
I booked it last night. Forgot to say. It's fine, I've got it in my calendar.
Of course you have 🙄
oh good i was going to do that tonight
No you weren't.
no i wasnt
Clinic's running forty minutes behind. Somebody has just asked me to look at a rash that is clearly a sunburn from October. Some people.
is it sunburn or did they go to Spain for a week and forget to tell the surgery
Spain. They're very proud of it.
bus broke down on the ring road, 40 mins with a load of pensioners and a man with a goat. dont ask
Was it a real goat?
it was a real goat helen
Girls want to know if the hat will still be there Saturday week. I said I'd ask
It'll still be there. It's been on that hook since 1998, it's not going anywhere.
see helen gets it
Thanks Helen. I'll tell them the hat is safe and Auntie Helen says so
Don't put my name on a hat.
argyle on tonight. anyone watching or are we pretending its not on
Can't, kids are still up, Mia has decided she's not going to sleep until she's seen a fox. Fox is in the garden. Long story
ha. say hi to the fox
Mark's watching it. He says we're 1-0 down and it's not even halftime. I'm going to bed.
night helen
they've equalised. lads on the bus are going mad
